now.detail: The hosted landing page now acts as a development dashboard with direct links to the emulator, device code, printer driver, product decisions, roadmap and live task snapshot.

next.why: Use the hosted pages on desktop or phone and send visual or interaction feedback through chat.

next.task: Decide what to do about print duration
next.why: A print takes about 56 seconds; 26.3 seconds is serial transfer at 9600 baud. Hardware-safe speed tests are the next useful experiment.

next.task: Exercise the d-pad in focus mode
next.why: The browser emulator now exposes the proposed control model at the real 176×264 panel shape and refresh timing.
Mount every component visibly, keep probe access, and make it mobile enough to use like a camera.

blocked.why: Bluetooth and WiFi must remain usable. Test pinned-clock mini-UART first; keep USB-serial as fallback.
Best decided after hands-on feedback from the hosted d-pad emulator.
Higher baud rates and heat timing must be proven on paper; software simulation cannot verify signal integrity or print density.

done.note: Responsive hosted landing page with important files, current tasks, system specs and roadmap.
Browser Floyd–Steinberg moved into a shared module and fixed input patterns are checked against Pillow.
1,338 generated files removed from tracking while remaining on the development machine.
A source starts live view; shutter freezes a frame and a second press resumes.
Selectable rotation and fill-mode crop; print output matches the preview framing.
Six hardware-free checks protect bitmap framing, packing, padding and validation.
Static project pages and emulator are hosted from docs/ on the public repository.
